why.label: Why This Trip?
why.title: 5 Reasons Why Istria Should Be Your Next Gourmet Destination

points.title: Truffle — Freshly Shaved Over Your Pasta
points.text: Join the Karlić family and their trained dogs in the hunt for world-renowned Istrian truffles — top specimens reach up to €4,000/kg. Afterward, cook and enjoy a 3-course meal together.

points.title: Olive Oil from the World's Best Region — 9 Years Running
points.text: Istria has been named the world's best olive oil region 9 consecutive times by Flos Olei. Taste the oils of Chiavalon, the Flos Olei "Producer of the Year."

points.title: Wines from "4 Soils" — One Malvazija, Four Characters
points.text: The "4 Soils" concept (red, white, grey, black earth) produces four distinct Malvazija characters. At Kozlović, winemakers since 1904, you'll taste the difference.

points.title: Farewell Dinner at Croatia's First Michelin Restaurant
points.text: Your final evening: dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in Rovinj — overlooking the Adriatic with a menu that gives Istrian traditions a modern twist. Included in Spirit of Istria.

points.title: An Abandoned Stone Village as Your Private Base
points.text: Kotli — a fully restored medieval village in the Mirna valley. 8 stone houses, pool, panoramic terrace. No neighbors. Just your group.

story.lead: Kotli is a hamlet of stone houses in the Mirna valley, in the heart of Istria, where the river drops through a chain of rock basins on its way to the sea.

chapters.title: The river
chapters.text: Kotli comes from kotao, Croatian for cauldron — the round basins the Mirna has hollowed into the stone. The water falls from one pool into the next, just below the houses.

chapters.title: The mill village
chapters.text: For centuries Kotli was the main mill village of the Hum region. Grain came down from the hills to be ground here, and the old mill still stands by the water.

chapters.title: Brought back to life
chapters.text: When the mills fell silent, the village emptied. Its stone houses have since been restored one by one, and today Kotli welcomes private groups all year and open weekends in winter.

story.caption: The Mirna at Kotli

houses.label: The stone houses
houses.title: Eight houses, one village
houses.text: Each house has its own living room, kitchen, bedroom and bathroom, with a fireplace for cool evenings. Guests share the pool, the terrace and the lanes between them.

meta.title: Hiking in Istria — 5 Days on Foot from a Stone Village | Kotli Retreat
meta.description: 5 days, 4 nights of guided walks through inland Istria: the Parenzana trail, the Glagolitic Alley to Hum, the Mirna valley and Motovun. Stone houses in Kotli, all meals included. Groups of 10–34.

hero.title: Istria on Foot
hero.subtitle: Five days of walking through the green heart of Istria
hero.poetic: Old railway lines, hilltop towns and a river that falls into stone basins — and a long table waiting at the end of every walk.
hero.season: All year · best in spring and autumn

days.title: Welcome to Kotli
days.narrative: You arrive in a stone village on the Mirna, where the river drops into the round basins that gave Kotli its name. A first short walk along the water, then dinner on the terrace.

days.narrative: Seven kilometres between two walled towns, past eleven stone monuments to the old Glagolitic script. You finish in Hum, the smallest town in the world, with lunch in its konoba.

days.title: The old railway to Motovun
days.narrative: The narrow-gauge line that once ran from Trieste to Poreč is now a trail of viaducts and tunnels. You walk the stretch below Motovun, then climb into the town for the view over the truffle forests.

days.narrative: A walk through the vineyards and oak woods of the Mirna valley that ends at the Kozlović winery, for a tasting of Malvazija and lunch with a view.

accommodation.title: Stone Houses in Kotli
accommodation.subtitle: A restored stone village on the Mirna, with trails starting at the door.
accommodation.intro: Kotli is a tiny stone village in the heart of Istria, where the Mirna river cascades into the basin-shaped hollows that gave the place its name. After a day on the trails you come back to your own stone house, a pool in summer and a fire in winter.

features.title: 8 Stone Houses
features.text: 80–140 m² houses with living room, kitchen, bedroom and bathroom. For 2–5 guests. Fireplace, Wi-Fi, private parking.

features.title: Pool and Fireplace
features.text: A pool for summer evenings and a fireplace in every house for the cooler months.

features.title: Dogs Welcome
features.text: Bring the dog on the walks (€10/day). The river paths start right outside.

features.title: Getting There
features.text: Pula Airport 1h · Trieste 1.5h · Ljubljana 2h · Munich 5h · Vienna 5h. Airport transfers on request.

points.title: Trails from the Door
points.text: The Mirna, the waterfalls and the old mill are a few steps from your house. Some days the walk starts right in the village.

points.title: Stories in Stone
points.text: The Glagolitic Alley and the walled towns of Roč and Hum: a thousand years of history on a seven-kilometre path.

points.title: An Old Railway
points.text: The Parenzana once carried trains from Trieste to Poreč. Today its viaducts and tunnels carry walkers and cyclists.

points.title: Lunch Where You Finish
points.text: Every walk ends at a table: a konoba in Hum, truffles below Motovun, Malvazija at Kozlović.

points.title: Paced for the Group
points.text: Routes of 7–12 km on easy to moderate paths. We shorten, lengthen or swap them to suit who's coming.

items.q: How fit do we need to be?
items.a: The walks are 7–12 km a day on easy to moderate paths with some climbs. Anyone who walks regularly will be fine. We can shorten any route or add an easier option.
Yes. A local guide walks with you every day, tells the stories along the way and knows where to stop.
Spring (March–June) and autumn (September–November) are ideal. Summer walks start early to avoid the heat, and winter days are cool and clear.
We move the walk to another day or swap it for a shorter route, a winery or a visit to a hilltop town.
No. Daily transport to every trailhead and back to Kotli is included. You only need to get to Kotli.

items.q: How big must the group be?
items.a: From 10 to 34 guests. For smaller groups, write to us and we'll see what we can do.

hero.poetic: Malvazija from four soils, Teran from red earth, Muškat in the Momjan hills — tasted where it grows, with the people who make it.

why.label: Why Istria
why.title: A small region with big wines

points.title: Malvazija from Four Soils
points.text: At Kozlović the same grape grows on four soils. Tasting them side by side shows why Istrian Malvazija is so varied.

points.title: Teran and Muškat
points.text: Teran from the red earth, sweet Muškat from the Momjan hills: two wines you rarely find outside Istria.

points.title: Families, Not Factories
points.text: Most Istrian wineries are family-run. You taste with the people who make the wine.

points.title: Food to Match
points.text: Truffles from the Karlić family, olive oil from Chiavalon and a winemaker's dinner in Kotli.

points.title: Nobody Drives
points.text: A driver takes you to every winery and back, so everyone can taste.

items.q: Do we need to know about wine?
items.a: No. The winemakers explain everything, and the tastings are relaxed. Wine clubs and beginners are equally welcome.
We do. Daily transport with a driver is included, so nobody has to drive after a tasting.
All year. September brings the harvest, spring the new Malvazija, and winter quiet cellars and lit fireplaces.

items.q: Can we buy wine to take home?
items.a: Yes, at every winery. Purchases aren't included in the price. We can help you ship larger orders.

items.q: What about guests who don't drink?
items.a: We prepare non-alcoholic pairings and local juices. Just tell us in your inquiry.

items.q: How big must the group be?
items.a: From 10 to 34 guests. For smaller groups, write to us and we'll see what we can do.
